name: Bless
effect: Choose any number of willing creatures in the area when the spell is cast. For the duration, affected creatures gain +5 TN for every rank in the caster's Domain [Covenant] skill on all tests for the duration. A creature cannot benefit from more than one Bless at a time.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::covenant::Bless

name: Command
effect:
Choose one visible living creature of Standard size or smaller within range that can hear and understand the caster. The caster utters a single clear one-word command such as Drop Item, Fall, Halt, Flee, Scream, or Surrender. The target must pass an Average (+0) Willpower test or, on its next Turn, spend 1 AP carrying out that command as literally and directly as possible. If it has no AP remaining when its Turn begins, it must spend the first AP it gains in the next Round doing so instead.

The command must be brief, physically possible, and not directly self-destructive. A commanded creature may still use AP to defend itself before its next Turn as normal. The spell does not grant control beyond that single compelled act.

Drop Item: release one held item. Fall : immediately go prone.
Halt: stop moving and take no movement on that compelled turn.
Flee: use that AP to move away from the caster by the safest obvious route.
Scream: waste the AP vocalizing. Surrender: triggers a Morale check

If the command is impossible, too complex, or would obviously require immediate self-harm, the spell has no effect beyond costing MP.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::covenant::Command

name: Continual Light
effect:
The caster fixes a globe of bright sacred light on a visible point, surface, or portable object within range. The illuminated area becomes a 7m-radius zone of full bright light and counts as sunlight for creatures, traits, and effects that are hindered or harmed by sunlight. The effect remains stationary unless fixed to a portable object, in which case it moves with that object. The caster may dismiss it as a Free Action.

If the caster targets an unwilling creature directly, that creature may pass a Willpower test; on a success, the light anchors to the nearest point directly behind or adjacent to the creature instead of upon it. If this effect overlaps with a magical darkness effect, the newer effect suppresses the older one while the overlap lasts. A Dispel effect of equal or higher spell level ends Continual Light
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::covenant::Continual Light

name: Detect Death
effect:
The caster opens their sight to the proper turning of life, death, decay, dormancy, and renewal. While the spell is maintained, they sense strong disturbances in that cycle within range.
This reveals undead, creatures or effects unnaturally preserved beyond their proper span, active magic that greatly hastens decay or aging within range. It does not reveal mundane malice, ordinary disease, poison, traps, or cursed items unless they are themselves being actively sustained by such a disruption.
The spell grants presence and direction, not exact analysis. The GM should describe each detected disturbance in Cycle-flavored terms such as stalled, overripe, withered, prematurely severed, or unnaturally returned.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::cycle::Detect Death

name: Fumble
effect:
The caster disrupts the target's place in the rhythm of motion, forcing body and intention out of sequence. When the spell takes effect, and again at the start of each affected creature's Turn while it remains in the area, that creature must pass an Average (+0) Willpower test or suffer the spell's effects until the start of its next Turn. While affected:

* all physical skill tests are treated as one difficulty harder
* the first time the creature fails an Athletics, Acrobatics, Combat Style, Evade, or similar physical test during that interval, it loses 1 AP
* if it has no AP remaining when this would occur, it instead cannot take Reactions until the start of its next Turn

Even simple physical acts done under pressure, such as picking up a dropped item, scrambling over a low obstacle, running stairs, or similar movements, may require an Athletics test at GM discretion while affected
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::cycle::Fumble

name: Haste
effect:
The caster pulls a creature forward along the wheel of exertion, letting it spend tomorrow's momentum in the present. While the spell is maintained, the target:

* doubles its Movement Rate
* gains +4 Initiative
* once on each of its Turns, after spending 1 AP on a Primary Action, may immediately either: resolve a different 1 AP Secondary Action for free, or move up to half its Speed

This extra effect cannot be used to:

* Cast Magic
* trigger another free action from this spell

This spell does not stack with itself
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::cycle::Haste

name: Aedric Spear
effect: The caster calls down a pillar of solar radiance upon one visible target within range. The attack deals 1d6 sunlight damage to the target.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::duty::Aedric Spear

name: Steadfast
effect: The caster and any number of willing allies in the area become immune to Panic, Horror, intimidation, and other non-magical mental or emotional coercion for the duration. In addition, affected creatures gain +20 TN on Willpower tests against magical fear, charm, domination, illusion-based mental manipulation, and similar mind-affecting effects. If an affected creature is already suffering such an effect when Steadfast is cast, it may immediately attempt one new Willpower test to end it.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::duty::Steadfast

name: Vigil of Duty
effect: Choose one willing target within range. For the duration, the target gains a bonus to all successful defensive tests equal to the caster's Ritual [Duty] rank.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::duty::Vigil of Duty

name: Magic Mouth
effect:
The caster places a speaking seal of bargain and reply upon one inanimate object. When a chosen trigger occurs within 10 m, a magical mouth appears upon the object and speaks a prepared phrase of up to 35 words, then the spell ends. The trigger must be based on a plainly observable condition, such as:

* a spoken word or phrase
* a creature entering a defined space
* a named item, token, or visible sum of coin being presented
* an item being placed into, removed from, opened, or touched upon the enchanted object

The trigger cannot depend on hidden intentions, invisible creatures, moral alignment, skill rank, or other qualities that cannot be discerned by ordinary senses.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::exchange::Magic Mouth

name: Slow
effect:
One visible target within range must pass a Willpower test or become slowed for the duration. A slowed target has its Speed halved, suffers -6 to Initiative, and reduces its maximum AP by 1 to a minimum of 1.
Slow does not stack with itself or similar magical speed-reduction effects. If the target is affected by a magical haste effect, whichever effect has the higher spell level suppresses the other while it remains active; if equal, both are canceled.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::exchange::Slow

name: Word of Recall
effect:
The caster instantly teleports to a pre-designated sanctuary point on the same plane: shrine, countinghouse, guildhall, vault, workshop, caravan-circle, temple side-chamber, or similar place that they have personally consecrated or registered during a 10-minute rite. The spell carries the caster, all worn and carried equipment, one willing touched creature of Standard size or smaller if that creature remains in contact throughout the casting, plus one additional creature for every spell level above 4.

The destination must be unoccupied and physically able to receive the travelers. If the destination is blocked, warded against teleportation, or no longer valid, the spell fails and the MP is lost. A character may maintain only one recall point. Designating a new point beyond that limit removes the oldest one.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::exchange::Word of Recall

name: Confusion
effect:
The caster snarls the immediate future around one enemy, forcing it to glimpse too many possible next moments at once. The target creature must pass an Average (+0) Willpower test or become fate-confused for the spell's duration. At the start of each affected creature's Turn, roll 1d100 and apply the result for that Turn:

* 01-10: Attack the caster if able. If not, move toward the caster by the most direct safe route.
* 11-50: Stand confused and take no purposeful Primary Action this Turn.
* 51-70: Attack the nearest enemy if able. If not, move toward that enemy.
* 71-80: Attack the nearest ally if able. If not, move toward that ally.
* 81-90: If unengaged, move directly away from the caster at walk speed and take no other purposeful action. If engaged, dither instead.
* 91-00: Act normally this Turn, but remain fate-confused until the spell ends or the effect is resisted off.

Each time a fate-confused creature is damaged by an attack, it may immediately make another Willpower test at +0 to end the spell's effect on itself. Large and bigger creatures make the initial and additional resistance tests at +20 TN.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::fate::Confusion

name: Hold Creature
effect:
The caster names the instant in which the target fails to move, and for a heartbeat destiny refuses to advance. A humanoid target within range must pass an Average(+0) Willpower test or become Paralyzed for the spell's duration.
While held by this spell, the target is completely helpless and cannot move, act, or defend itself. Nothing short of an appropriate magical release, dispelling the effect, or the spell ending releases the target early.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::fate::Hold Creature

name: Blind
effect: The caster cuts the chosen target off from the world's next revealed moment, and sight gives way to blank, omenless darkness. One visible creature within range is immediately afflicted with the Blinded condition for 1 round.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::fate::Blind

name: Change Appearance
effect:
The caster cloaks themselves in a refined illusion that alters their apparent form into any humanoid or person-shaped biped of roughly similar mass. The illusion may alter height, build, sex, face, hair, clothing, and carried gear, and grants +20 TN on tests to pass as the chosen appearance under casual inspection.

This spell does not alter the caster's scent, voice, or physical substance. A creature that touches the caster, closely inspects them at arm's length, or has strong reason for suspicion gains +20 TN on Observe tests made to detect the deception.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::grace::Change Appearance

name: Graceful Step
effect:
One willing target within range moves with impossible poise and grace for the duration. The target ignores penalties from difficult terrain and similar hindrances, and may move and fight unimpeded by unusual combat scenarios (p.102 Rules Compendium) without the usual movement or weapon penalties.

In addition, the target reduces movement and action penalties imposed by magical hindrance effects by 20 TN, to a minimum penalty of 0. If an effect would leave the target unable to move at all, the target may immediately repeat the relevant resistance test with a +20 TN bonus; on a success, that immobilizing effect is suppressed for as long as Graceful Step is maintained.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::grace::Graceful Step

name: Mirror Image
effect:
Three shifting illusory doubles appear around the caster, mimicking their movements and making their exact position hard to judge.

Whenever a creature makes an attack that specifically targets the caster and does not ignore illusions, randomly determine whether the attack targets the caster or one of the remaining images before the attack is resolved:

* 3 images remaining: target the caster on 1 on 1d4
* 2 images remaining: target the caster on 1 on 1d3
* 1 image remaining: target the caster on 1 on 1d2

If an image is targeted, it vanishes and the attack misses automatically. If the caster is targeted, resolve the attack normally. The images move with the caster, copy visible wounds and gestures, and cannot attack, block movement, flank, trigger reactions, or satisfy effects that require a real body.
Area effects, pulse effects, and attacks that do not specifically target the caster are not intercepted by the images. Creatures or effects immune to illusions, or that explicitly ignore illusions, are unaffected by this spell.
Destroyed images are not restored by upkeep. Once all images are gone, the spell ends immediately
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::grace::Mirror Image

name: Purify Food and Drink
effect: All food and drink within the area is purified of rot, spoilage, mundane poison, foulness, and similar contamination. One casting is enough to cleanse roughly one day's provisions for three Standard creatures, or an equivalent quantity of liquid in waterskins, jugs, bowls, or a small cask. If the area contains blessed or holy water that has been corrupted, its sacred properties are restored.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::hearth::Purify Food and Drink

name: Cure Wounds
effect:
Choose one living target within 1m and one specific wound affecting one of its hit locations. That wound is immediately treated, and the target regains 10 HP in the chosen location. These HP may only be applied to that location and only count toward curing the chosen wound.

If, after this healing, the total HP restored toward that wound is equal to or greater than the damage that created it, the wound and all its effects end immediately. If the wound is not fully cured, its passive wound effects ( including crippled and maimed) are suppressed and blood-loss collapse is forestalled for 1 hour. This spell cannot restore a lost limb or remove an already maimed result.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::hearth::Cure Wounds

name: Spiritual Guardian
effect:
A luminous spiritual guardian manifests within 5m of the caster: a saintly sentinel, ancestor-protector or similar according to the domain's imagery. While the spell lasts, the caster may spend 1 AP on their Turn to direct the guardian to move up to 10m to a point they can see and make one melee attack against a target within 2m of it.

The attack uses the caster's casting skill for this spell. On a hit, the guardian deals 1d8+1 Crushing , Slashing or Splitting magic damage. The guardian may be Parried, Blocked, or Evaded as though it were a weapon-like attacker, but attacks directed against the guardian itself have no effect. If the spell ends, the guardian vanishes immediately.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::hearth::Spiritual Guardian

name: Magic Missile
effect:
The caster shapes three missiles of force. Each missile must target a visible creature within range and hits automatically unless the target is in total cover. A missile deals casters' Ritual [Domain] skill rank of magic damage to a random hit location and each separate missile has Crushing, Slashing and Splitting damage.

The caster may direct all missiles at one target or divide them among several targets, declaring targets before damage is rolled. A target can still defend against the missile with a defensive reaction.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::knowledge::Magic Missile

name: Know Languages
effect: Choose one touched sapient creature, text, inscription, or other written object. For the duration, the caster understands the meaning of any non-magical spoken or written language used by that subject. This allows comprehension of speech, script, symbols used as language, and ordinary encoded phrasing, but it does not grant the ability to speak, write, or flawlessly imitate the language.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::knowledge::Know Languages

name: Mage Sight
effect:
The caster creates a tiny invisible arcane eye and may perceive through it for the duration. The eye begins within 1m of the caster and may be guided to move up to 10m at the start of each of the caster's turns to any point the caster can trace a path through open space. The eye cannot pass through solid matter, fits through openings as small as a finger-width, and sees normally out to 20m.
While using the eye, the caster may make Observe tests from the eye's position instead of their own. The eye is unaffected by the caster's blindness, darkness around the caster, or similar hindrances affecting the caster's own physical senses, but gaze attacks or magical effects perceived through the eye still affect the caster normally. If the caster dismisses the spell, the eye disappears.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::knowledge::Mage Sight

name: Predict Weather
effect: The caster gains a forecast of the natural weather within roughly 40 km of their current location for the next 48 hours. This forecast includes temperature, precipitation, snowfall, wind strength, fog, and any major natural weather shift likely to occur in that period. If supernatural weather currently affects the area, the caster senses that the forecast is unreliable beyond the point where the unnatural effect begins or ends.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::nature::Predict Weather

name: Pet
effect:
One Beast or Bestial creature of Standard size or smaller and Intelligence 20 or lower must pass a Willpower test or fall under the caster's direct mental guidance for the duration. While the spell lasts, the caster may spend AP normally to direct the creature to move, scout, fetch, track, carry small objects, or perform other simple but purposeful tasks within its natural capabilities.

While maintaining the spell, the caster may choose to perceive through the creature's senses instead of their own, using its sight, hearing, smell, and similar senses; while doing so, the caster is treated as unaware of their own immediate surroundings beyond touch and obvious pain. If the target is already a loyal trained companion of the caster, it does not resist.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::nature::Pet

name: Speak with Beasts
effect:
For the duration, the caster may communicate with any Beast or Bestial creature capable of some form of signaling or expression, whether by sound, posture, scent, movement, instinctive imagery, or other natural mode. The caster speaks in their own language and is understood; the creature's responses are perceived by the caster in an intelligible form suited to its nature.
This spell does not compel honesty, friendliness, obedience, or human-like reasoning. A beast answers according to its instincts, memory, temperament, and immediate interests. The caster may shift from one creature to another of the same general kind during the duration without recasting the spell
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::nature::Speak with Beasts

name: Curse
effect: Each unwilling creature in the area must pass a Willpower test or suffer -5 TN for every rank in the caster's Domain [Covenant] skill on all tests for the duration. Multiple Curse effects do not stack.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::ruin::Curse

name: Cause Disease
effect:
The caster lays a wasting blight upon a visible creature within range, calling rot and weakness into flesh, blood, or spirit. The target must pass an Average (0) Endurance test or contract a magical disease chosen randomly.
A disease inflicted by this spell cannot be cured through ordinary treatment or the Healing skill alone. It may only be removed by appropriate magic, divine intervention, or other specifically suitable supernatural remedies.
If the target is already suffering from a disease when struck by this spell, the caster may instead choose to supplant that affliction by the disease rolled on the d100.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::ruin::Cause Disease

name: Bestow Curse
effect:
The caster marks the target for decline, drawing one thread of failure tight around them. A visible creature within range must pass an Average(+0) Willpower test or suffer one of the following curses, chosen by the caster, for as long as the spell is maintained:

* Withered Body: All tests using Strength or Endurance are one grade harder. The target suffers -2 Initiative and reduces physical damage dealt by 2.
* Blighted Mind: All tests using Intelligence, Willpower, or Personality are one grade harder. The target suffers -2 Initiative.
* Doomed Hand: The first failed test the target makes on each of its Turns is treated as a critical failure if the circumstances could reasonably permit one.

A target may only be affected by one instance of Bestow Curse at a time. A newer casting replaces an older one.

# Clerical Hierarchies

Clerical Hierarchies represent a character's formal rank within the religious structure of their faith, whether as part of the clergy or a recognized fighting order. These ranks do not provide any bonuses. Instead, they indicate the character's place within the domain doctrine, the degree of authority and respect they are likely to command among the faithful, and the level of ritual knowledge, training, and clerical responsibility normally expected of them. In practice, higher circles reflect greater standing within the faith, but rank does not always correspond perfectly to personal influence, office, or individual capability.

| Circle Rank | Priesthood | Fighting Orders |
| :---: | :---: | :---: |
| I | - | Aspirant |
| II | Priest | Knight-Errant |
| III | Prelate | Commander |
| IV | Archbishop | Grandmaster |
| V | Primate | - |
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::ruin::Bestow Curse

name: Web
effect:
The caster calls down strands of dusk-woven webbing that spill across the chosen point and cling to bodies, weapons, and the ground alike. Creatures in the area must pass an Evade test or become webbed. A webbed creature is Entangled and Immobilized.
On its Turn, a webbed creature may spend 1 AP to attempt to break free with an opposed Strength or Athletics test against the spell. The web has 2 AR and 6 Hit Points. Fire damage ignores the web's Armor Points.
While the spell is maintained, the web remains and continues to hinder movement through the area as difficult terrain, even for creatures that were not originally caught.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::twilight::Web

name: Darkvision
effect:
The caster grants the touched target sight fit for the border between day and night. While the spell is maintained, the recipient can see clearly in darkness out to 20 m.
This sight functions through mundane darkness and dim light, and allows the target to ignore penalties from poor illumination within range. It does not see through solid objects, thick fog, magical blindness, or effects that specifically block supernatural sight.
If the target is already in an area created by Darkness, this spell still allows them to see normally through that spell's effect.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::twilight::Darkvision

name: Darkness
effect:
The caster spreads a globe of thick twilight that swallows brightness and muffles clear sight. The area becomes one of total magical darkness.
Creatures without a supernatural means of seeing through darkness are treated as unable to see within the area. Mundane light sources are completely suppressed while inside it. Lesser magical lights are also smothered at the GM's discretion.
A creature benefiting from Darkvision can see through this spell normally. If Light and Darkness overlap, the more recently applied effect overrides the other in the overlapping area for as long as it remains active. This spell does not stack with itself
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::twilight::Darkness

name: Battle Chant
effect: The caster intones a battle-chant that fills the area around them. While the chant is maintained, the caster and all willing allies within range add the caster's Ritual [Domain] skill rank to the physical damage they deal.
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::victory::Battle Chant

name: True Weapon
effect: One touched, wielded melee weapon is sanctified for the duration. Whenever its wielder rolls damage with that weapon, if any of the weapon's base damage dice show a result of 1, each such die may be rerolled once. In addition, the weapon counts as one size category larger for the purpose of overcoming parries
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::victory::True Weapon

name: Blade Barrier
effect:
The caster creates a stationary 2m-radius barrier of whirling spectral blades centered on a visible point within range. Whenever a creature enters the area for the first time on a Turn or starts its Turn inside the barrier, it suffers 1d6 Slashing Magic damage to a random hit location.

The blades are too dense and violent to be Parried or Evaded, though a shield may still protect hit locations passively as normal. When the barrier first appears, any creature already inside it and within 1m of the outer edge may attempt an Evade test to throw itself clear. On a success, it is placed prone just outside the barrier and suffers no damage. On a failure, it is still thrown prone just outside the barrier, but suffers the spell's damage first
sourcePath: docs/Core/The Annotated Anuad of Worship.md::Domain Spells::victory::Blade Barrier
